title: All‑staff sprint pulse playbook and exec penumbra v0.1
content:
Context and intent:
This note is a compact playbook for the cross-company sprint pulse we want to run ahead of the Q2 cadence reset and the all-staff. Purpose: 1) give Exec a crisp update frame (the "penumbra" narrative below) they can use in town; 2) surface one high-confidence ask per org for the next 6 weeks; 3) set lightweight decision triggers and contingencies so teams know when to escalate.

Quick framing — the Penumbra narrative (for Exec intros):
- High level: we are transitioning from build‑mode to operational‑scale mode. The "penumbra" is the set of near-term operational risks that live between product velocity and platform stability. We want to acknowledge the shadow (tradeoff choices) while signaling confidence that we have concrete mitigations.
- One sentence for town: "We shipped critical scaling features last quarter; now we are shifting focus to reliability, predictable unit costs, and developer ergonomics so customers can safely scale. Expect targeted capacity and cost wins in the next two releases, plus a tighter rollout plan for Dedicated/PVT offerings."

Executive snapshot (3 bullets, 30s):
- Customer momentum: self-serve usage up 38% QoQ; two mid-market trials (ACME/Polaris) moved to pilot stage with Dedicated requests.
- Platform metrics: median request P99 down 18% across hosted catalog, error rate stable at 0.6% (target <0.5%). We have three mitigations in flight (KV cache tuning, continuous batching update, fallback routing policy).
- Ask: runway and focus — freeze non-critical API surface changes for 4 weeks; prioritize Dedicated capacity autoscale fixes and rollout docs.

Draft OKRs (proposal — numeric where possible)
Objective A: Make inference predictable and cheaper for scale customers (owner: Eng + Product)
- KR A1: Reduce median hosted request latency from ~120ms to <=95ms for 90% of traffic by end of Q2.
- KR A2: Reduce per‑token infrastructure spend by 12% on average across top 20 models through batching + cache improvements.
- KR A3: Add transparent per-model performance profiles in Console for top 10 models (adopted by 80% of internal evals).

Objective B: Strengthen reliability and rollout hygiene (owner: SRE + Console)
- KR B1: Lower customer-facing error rate from 0.6% to <=0.35% for hosted API.
- KR B2: Ship canary rollout tooling + automatic fallback policy and exercise it in 3 production rollouts.
- KR B3: Create runbooks for Dedicated and Private with SLA play tests (one exercise per month).

Objective C: Improve product-led conversion and retention (owner: Growth + DX)
- KR C1: Improve free-tier -> paid conversion by 20% through usage nudges and targeted onboarding flows.
- KR C2: Increase retention (30-day active) for teams running >10k tokens/day by 15% with curated model & config presets.

All-hands run-of-show (compact)
- 0:00–0:05 Welcome + founders note (Penumbra frame — short, human).
- 0:05–0:12 Exec update (three bullets above + 1 slide of metrics).
- 0:12–0:25 Team spotlight (SRE: canary demo + fallback policy).
- 0:25–0:40 Interactive labs (breakouts): each org picks 1 play to commit to (shown below).
- 0:40–0:50 Q&A + escalation throughput (pre-submitted prompts via Slido).
- 0:50–1:00 Commit and close (each lead posts top ask in #all-hands-asks).

Breakout lab prompts (for facilitators):
- Eng/Serving-runtime: pick one latency improvement and list blockers; define quick experiment (owner: Ravi).
- Product/Console: identify top two confusing UX flows for Dedicated onboarding; propose fixes.
- SRE: select a canary scenario and validate rollback policy end-to-end.
- Growth/DX: design one conversion nudge experiment tied to a product config.

One-ask per org (draft list — to finalize before all-hands)
- Eng-serving-runtime: complete KV cache auto-eviction rollout and shipping metrics (owner: Samir).
- Console/Observability: publish per-route token cost visualization and alerting (owner: Elena).
- Private deployments: finalize KMS integration checklist for on-prem installs (owner: Priya).
- Growth: A/B for onboarding 'first-API-success' to increase conversion (owner: Deniz).

Decision triggers and contingency playbook (operational)
- Trigger 1 — sustained client P99 degradation >25% for 12 hours: escalate to SRE + notify sales CS; enable temporary traffic routing to Dedicated region.
- Trigger 2 — unexpected quota spike >3x baseline for 6 hours: throttle new signups for free tier, open immediate capacity incident.
- Trigger 3 — critical security or compliance gap surfaced in audit: pause new Private deployments until mitigation validated.
- Each trigger maps to a short checklist (pager, rollback step, customer comm owner). Placeholders: SRE Pager rotation doc -> Confluence.

Risks and mitigations (notes to self)
- Risk: Batching changes could increase tail latency for small interactive workloads. Mitigation: dual-path routing by workload signature + synthetic monitoring across buckets.
- Risk: Over-indexing on cost KRs might harm quality (regressions). Mitigation: tie cost wins to quality checks + regression alarms on small eval prompts.
- Risk: All-hands asks feel heavy; teams won't follow through. Mitigation: require commit message in #all-hands-asks with owner + 2-line plan within 48 hours.

Operational checklist for the next 6 weeks
- Week 0 (now): freeze non-critical API surface changes; push the "penumbra" slide into the all-hands deck (owner: Maya).
- Week 1–2: execute three high-confidence infra experiments (KV tuning, batching tweak, fallback routing). Capture before/after metrics.
- Week 3–4: roll canary and run SLA play tests for Dedicated.
- Week 5–6: run cross-org retrospective; capture decisions and convert to OKR commitments.

Open questions (to resolve before townhall)
- What is the minimal set of per-model metrics to show in Console that will satisfy both Growth and SRE? (Product + SRE sync: RW-9182).
- Is the freeze broad enough? Which API surfaces are "critical" and exempt? Need Exec sign-off.
- Do we need a customer-facing note about expected capacity improvements and potential short-term flakiness? (CS + Legal).

Next steps and owners (immediate)
- Maya: finalize slide deck and circulate two pager to Exec by Thu EOD.
- Ravi: draft experiment plan for KV/cache and post to RW-9123 by Mon.
- Elena: prepare Console mock showing per-route cost tile; quick usability test with two customers.
- Samir: confirm SRE runbook pages and on-call coverage for the all-hands weekend.

Notes and references (internal links):
- See RW-9123 (KV cache experiment), RW-9182 (Console metric scope), infra PR #278 (autoscale prototype).
- Slack channels: #eng-serving-runtime, #sre-ops, #product-console, #all-hands-asks.

Appendix: quick draft of the 2‑pager for Exec (copyable)
Subject: Q2 operational posture + focused asks
- We shipped major scaling infra last quarter; this quarter our job is to turn capability into predictable customer outcomes: lower latency, lower unit cost, and confident rollouts for Dedicated/Private.
- We propose a temporary four-week freeze on non-critical API surface changes to avoid churn while we execute three infra experiments and run canary rollouts.
- Specific asks: Exec approval on freeze; prioritized headcount for the Dedicated rollout sprint (2 infra engineers for 6 weeks); a lightweight customer note approved by CS/Legal.

---
This is intentionally concise. Will iterate in next pass; please add edits inline and mark anything that must be in the final-slide pack.
